title: Introduce invocation ticker and alert decay controller
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Added invocation-ticker metrics, an alert decay controller to reduce alert noise for rapidly recurring invocation fingerprints, and a new dashboard panel for live ticker streams. No user-facing API changes.
description:
Motivation: We currently see alert churn for bursty invocation patterns where many similar invocations repeatedly trigger the same SLO alerts within a short window. Root cause analysis shows many such alerts are transient and dominated by the same invocation fingerprints (hot prompts). This PR implements two complementary pieces: 1) a lightweight per-invocation ticker that emits stage-aligned heartbeat metrics so we can understand phase durations without full trace hydration, and 2) an alert decay controller that dampens alert signal for repeated fingerprints over a configurable decay window.

What this PR does (high level):
- Introduces a new metric set: redwood.invocation.ticker.duration_ms (histogram), redwood.invocation.ticker.stage (gauge labels: start/kernels/kv/cache/emit), redwood.invocation.ticker.status (counter: started/completed/failed).
- Adds redwood.alert.decay_score (gauge) and redwood.alert.decay_events_total which power the decay controller logic.
- Implements a pluggable AlertDecayController that subscribes to fingerprint counts from the agg layer and applies a decay multiplier to alert weights exposed to the alerting pipeline. The controller runs per-tenant and honors TTL and minimum floor thresholds.
- Adds a lightweight in-process ticker generator in the serving runtime. The generator emits minimal payloads (stage, elapsed_ms, invocation_fingerprint) to the metrics relay; it is turned off by default and can be enabled per-tenant via runtime config.
- Adds an observability dashboard (Invocation Ticker Stream & Alert Decay) with a live stream panel, fingerprint heatmap, and decay effectiveness view.
- Adds unit and integration tests for decay scoring and the ticker's stage transitions.

Why this approach:
- Full trace enrichment is expensive; a ticker gives a low-cardinality, cheap signal aligned to stages (prefix warmup, kernel queue, generation, post-processing) that is actionable for SRE and product.
- Decaying alert weight instead of hard-suppressing alerts preserves fidelity (we still record incidents) but lowers alert noise so oncall can focus on novel or persistent regressions.

Implementation notes: (single continuous description) The AlertDecayController maintains an LRU-backed fingerprint ledger with time-decayed scores. When an alert candidate arrives it is annotated with a decay_multiplier in [0.1,1.0] based on recent fingerprint activity; the alert router multiplies signal weight by this multiplier and only escalates if weighted score passes thresholds. Decay parameters are configurable via the existing observability configstore and default to a 10-minute half-life with a minimum floor of 0.25. The ticker is implemented as a non-blocking ring buffer inside the request worker; emission is batched to the metrics relay via the telemetry client. To limit cardinality we only publish the 64-bit fingerprint hash (not raw prompt) and expose a tenant-level sample rate.

Checklist:
- [x] Metric names and docs added (telemetry/metrics.md)
- [x] Runtime opt-in flag and tenant config
- [x] Alert router integration and decay multiplier plumbing
- [x] Dashboard JSON and runbook snippets
- [x] Unit tests for decay math and ticker state machine
- [x] Integration test that verifies reduced alert fires under simulated burst

Testing performed:
- Local unit tests: tick-state transitions and decay math (100% coverage for new modules)
- Integration: stressbench harness that simulates 10k invocations/min with 30% fingerprint reuse; alert fires dropped by ~78% while detection latency for persisted regressions remained < 2% worse.
- E2E in staging: enabled ticker for a single tenant for 48h; verified telemetry pipeline ingestion throughput increased by <2% and no regression in token-latency SLOs.

Operational concerns & fallbacks:
- The ticker is disabled by default in production; enablement is per-tenant. If telemetry relay backpressure occurs the emission is automatically sampled down and metric emissions are dropped with a counter.
- The decay controller logs a provenance event for any alert it attenuates so runbooks can identify suppressed incidents.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge and deploy server-side with ticker disabled. 2) Enable ticker+decay for internal QA tenants and run 48-hour validation (observability/qa). 3) Gradual ramp to high-traffic tenants with monitoring on redwood.alert.decay_effectiveness and redwood.alert.suppressed_total.

Docs & runbook: Added runbook section that explains when to tune half-life and floor, and how to disable decay per-alert.

notes_for_ops:
If enabling for a tenant, monitor redwood.alert.suppressed_total and redwood.alert.decay_effectiveness. If suppression is too aggressive, increase floor parameter or shorten half-life. Use scripts/staging/ticker-enable.sh to toggle.
Runbook link: runbooks/alert_decay.runbook.md
